newsitem.title: UK: European air cargo users resist fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: European air cargo users resist fuel surcharge.

text.p: European air cargo customers are strongly resisting surcharges imposed by major airlines due to higher jet fuel costs, European Air Shippers Council secretary general, Chris Welsh said.

"The surcharges are being strongly resisted by national shipper (exporters and manufacturers) organisations, following a tremendous backlash from some individual shippers," he said in telephone interview from Brussels.

Major airlines - mainly from Europe and led by Germany's Deutsche Lufthansa AG - began announcing surcharges on October 25. The surcharge is generally equivalent to US10 cents a kg, applicable worldwide, with differences on certain routes.

The EASC has written to the International Air Transport Association(IATA),"to express our serious concern at the sudden imposition of surcharges which has caused considerable problems for exporters and asking them what they intend to do about these problems," Welsh said.

"Information from our members suggests there is a strong case of over-recovery (of costs). Feedback from France and the Netherlands clearly suggests this over-recovery, as French transatlantic costs appear to have gone up 10 pct," Welsh added

"In the past three months, airline fuel costs have risen around 30 percent. As these represent around 10 to 11 percent of overall costs, a three percent surcharge would reflect the real increase," he said.
Most of the surcharges were imposed with little warning. Lufthansa's came into force on November 1 while British Airways Plc surcharge was announced on October 31 and takes effect on November 8.
IATA is holding an emergency meeting of its 254 member airlines in Geneva on November 13 to consider "concerted action" to counter rising fuel costs for cargo and passenger traffic.

"We have also had informal contacts with the European Commission to alert them to the potential problem. Any formal approach will depend on the information and views we receive from our members and what action is then decided," Welsh added.
The EASC represents all countries in Western Europe with the exception of Austria, Italy, Portugal, Greece, Turkey and Malta
It has also approached airfreight forwarders, through FIATA, their international association based in Zurich and via their national organisations.
In several countries, including France, Germany and the Netherlands, shippers and forwarders have joined forces to make strong protests to the carriers imposing the surcharge, Welsh said.

Industry sources said there is a further twist to the situation in that when a national carrier introduces a surcharge, other airlines with services from that carrier's country also tend to follow its example.
When BA announced a surcharge on freight leaving the UK, Thai Airways followed with a similar rise even though Thai had not introduced a global surcharge at that stage.

"The sudden imposition of a surcharge, in many cases with virtually no warning, is unacceptable in today's trading environment. Manufacturers and exporters need a reasonable period to negotiate such increases," Welsh added.
"As matters stand today and given the short notice, most will be unable to recover the cost from their customers," he said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
